> Synthetic document written for a demo. All names, codes and figures are
> invented. Clause ids are stable across versions; a retired clause never
> comes back under the same id. Where a project annex covers a point, the
> annex applies.

## WP-1.1 Scope
This procedure applies to every warehouse of the Organization, WH-01 to
WH-40, and to every project that holds stock in them. Each project annex
adds the rules that differ by donor-funded project.

## WP-2.1 Movement ledger
Every receipt, dispatch, transfer and write-off is recorded in the movement
ledger. The ledger is only ever appended to: an entry is never edited or
deleted. A wrong quantity is corrected with a new adjusting movement that
refers to the original entry.

## WP-2.2 Separate project stock
Balances are kept per warehouse, per project, per item and per expiry date.
Stock of different projects stored in the same building must never be
merged, even for the same item code.

## WP-3.1 Receiving
Every receipt needs a goods received note (RCV) issued from a purchase order
or, for an in-kind donation, under the project annex that accepts donations.

## WP-3.2 Counting in pieces
Quantities are recorded in pieces. Boxes are converted with the item's
pieces-per-box figure, so 12 boxes + 6 pieces of an item packed 24 per box
is recorded as 294 pieces.

## WP-4.1 First expired, first out
When the same item is held in batches with different expiry dates, issue
the batch with the earliest expiry date first (FEFO).

## WP-4.2 No negative balance
A dispatch or transfer that would take a balance below zero is refused.
Dispatch only what is in stock and record the remainder as pending on the
waybill.

## WP-6.1 Damage report
Damaged stock is recorded on a damage report (DMG) with a written incident
description and photos where possible. A damage report becomes a write-off
only when the operations manager approves it. The project annex says who
else must sign above a quantity.

## WP-6.2 Expired stock
Expired stock must never be dispatched. Move it to the quarantine area and
record it on a damage report for the operations manager to approve its
write-off and disposal.
